newsitem.title: USA: Nissan says franchise damage permanent.
newsitem.headline: Nissan says franchise damage permanent.

text.p: Nissan Motor Corp USA, a unit of Japanese automaker Nissan Motor Co Ltd, said on Friday that a Virginia dealer's use of a racial slur to describe a black employee was "deplorable" and led the automaker to cancel its franchise agreement.

Bob Crumpler, the owner of Nissan dealerships in Newport News and Portsmouth, Va., was secretly videotaped referring to a black worker at the Newport News location as a "nigger." A local television station aired the tape.

"We found Mr. Crumpler's statements to be deplorable and reprehensive," Nissan Public Affairs Manager Kurt von Zumwalt told Reuters in a telephone interview from Los Angeles, "and that will not stand in the Nissan organization."
He said the automaker delivered a termination letter on Dec. 11 to Crumpler, who has 90 days to respond.
"The damage done to reputation -- to ours and to his -- can't be undone," von Zumwalt said.
Nissan has reprimanded Crumpler before for assaulting a police officer, but under its dealer agreement could not take action for the misdemeanor charge.

"This most recent action is a breach of contract because part of our dealer agreement is that the dealer shall not adversly impact the reputation of Nissan, the dealer or Nissan products," according to von Zumwalt.
Crumpler was not reachable for comment.
